title: SMTO-BOOT-0027 — This computer's processor type isn't supported by the vLLM installer
summary: The vLLM installer only works on Linux computers with x86_64 (common Intel and AMD) or aarch64 (64-bit ARM) processors. This computer reported a different type, so the installer stopped before installing vLLM.

html:
SMTO-BOOT-0027 — This computer's processor type isn't supported by the vLLM installer

GUID: 21a83e08-c938-42c2-b28c-0ee8795ad786
Slug: boot-vllm-arch-unsupported
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: boot

What happened

  • The vLLM installer only works on Linux computers with x86_64 (common Intel and AMD) or aarch64 (64-bit ARM) processors. This computer reported a different type, so the installer stopped before installing vLLM.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look at the line starting with "CPU:" just above the message. It shows the processor type the installer saw. That processor type is what this check rejected; the installer needs x86_64 or aarch64.
  2. Run uname -m. If it also shows something other than x86_64 or aarch64, run the installer on a Linux computer (or WSL) with an x86_64 or aarch64 processor. Ready-made vLLM packages exist only for these two processor types.
  3. If uname -m shows x86_64 or aarch64 but the "CPU:" line doesn't, set CONDA_HOME to a folder that doesn't exist yet, for example $HOME/miniforge3-smto, and run the installer again. The installer checks the processor through Conda's Python. A Conda made for another processor type reports the wrong one, and a fresh Conda will match this computer.

What success looks like

  • The "CPU:" line shows x86_64 or aarch64, and the installer goes on to print "Creating environment".

If it still fails

  • Copy the full terminal output, including the SMTO-BOOT-0027 line, plus the output of uname -m, and send it to the person who manages your model setup. Don't try to force the install by picking a vLLM package by hand; it won't run on this processor.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • vllm_install_support.py check_hardware rejected the Python-reported CPU architecture (platform.machine()) because it is neither x86_64 nor aarch64.

What this means

  • Wheel selection hardware validation finds a CPU architecture outside x86_64 and aarch64. Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.

Why this can happen

  • Wheel selection hardware validation finds a CPU architecture outside x86_64 and aarch64.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare platform.machine and Python/OS build with the selector's supported host families.

How to fix it

  • Run on Linux x86_64 or aarch64 with a Conda base Python built for that architecture. install-vllm.sh already rejects other uname -m values (boot_platform_unsupported), so via the installer this means $CONDA_BASE/bin/python -c 'import platform; print(platform.machine())' disagrees with uname -m (for example an emulated or 32-bit Conda): point CONDA_HOME at a matching Conda, or at an unused path so a matching Miniforge is installed. Do not bypass the check; the wheel selector supports no other architecture.
  • Use a supported x86_64 or aarch64 Linux host and supported Python/build.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported host/build is used without pretending a mismatched wheel is compatible.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass the unsupported-feature check or reinterpret an unsupported response as success.

Technical notes

  • Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
